executive_summary: The apply-state verifier's case-folding/implicit-cast/quote-scoping fix (SD-LEO-INFRA-APPLY-STATE-VERIFIER-001, PR #8973 + 2 adversarial rounds) has nothing stopping it from regressing. Freeze the sole confirmed false positive plus the real known-applied population that actually exercises the normalizer (150 function/trigger-declaring files, corrected from the SD's miscited ~124) as a DB-free CI regression corpus.

functional_requirements.requirement: A one-time (not CI-invoked) generator script that resolves the exact 150 function/trigger-declaring known-applied migration files (via lib/migration-audit-reader.js's listApplied({success:true,limit:1000}) + normalizeMigrationPath(), fs.existsSync, and a CREATE FUNCTION/CREATE TRIGGER regex -- the identical method LEAD Explore/VALIDATION independently verified twice, 393/388/366/150), extracts each file's own declaration text via scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs's exported extractFunctionBodies()/extractTriggerDefs(), queries the live DB for the corresponding prosrc / pg_get_triggerdef(oid,true) text (the same queries resolveLive() already issues), and writes ONE frozen JSON fixture file with an entry per object: {id, class, name, source_migration_path, file_text, live_text, captured_at}. The entry for trg_sd_mutation_audit (database/chairman-gated/20260912_sd_mutation_audit_actor_threading.sql) additionally carries confirmed_false_positive:true and a note citing SD-LEO-INFRA-AUDIT-ACTOR-THREADING-001 and SD-LEO-INFRA-APPLY-STATE-VERIFIER-001.
functional_requirements.description: This is the corpus's only live-DB touchpoint. Running it once (or on demand, when a real schema change legitimately moves a fixture) produces a fixture that then needs no live database ever again -- matching the SD scope's explicit 'CI needs no live database' requirement.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: The generated fixture's entry count is internally consistent with what the generator itself measures on the run that produced it (logged in the fixture's own provenance) -- NOT hard-coded to LEAD phase's historical count of 150, since schema_migrations_applied grows continuously in this active fleet and the true count at EXEC-generation time may differ; EXEC's PR evidence reports the actual count achieved.
AC-2: Exactly one entry (trg_sd_mutation_audit) carries confirmed_false_positive:true.
AC-3: Each entry's file_text is extracted via the existing extractFunctionBodies()/extractTriggerDefs() exports, never re-implemented ad hoc.

AC-4: Each entry's live_text is captured via the existing resolveLive() export (or an identical query shape, including its DISTINCT ON p.oid / t.oid tiebreak) -- never a hand-rolled SQL query that could silently drift from the query shape the real verifier issues in production, which would invalidate the corpus's fidelity to what it claims to regression-guard.

functional_requirements.requirement: A Vitest suite that loads the frozen fixture with zero database connection and, for every entry, replays the SAME comparison classifyFiles() performs internally: function entries via normalizeSqlBody(file_text) === normalizeSqlBody(live_text); trigger entries via normalizeTriggerWhenClause(extractTriggerWhenClause(file_text) ?? '') === normalizeTriggerWhenClause(extractTriggerWhenClause(live_text) ?? ''). Every entry must assert equal (the verifier's real-world APPLIED verdict for a currently-correctly-classified file). A dedicated, separately-labeled test asserts this for the confirmed_false_positive entry specifically, referencing its historical BODY_MISMATCH-to-APPLIED flip.
functional_requirements.description: This is the actual regression guard: if a future change to normalizeSqlBody()/normalizeTriggerWhenClause() reintroduces case-sensitivity, cast-sensitivity, or breaks quote-scoping (either adversarial-round fix), at least one of the 150 real fixtures will flip from equal to not-equal and fail CI immediately.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: All 150 fixture entries pass (comparison reads equal) against the current, correct normalizer implementation.
AC-2: The suite imports normalizeSqlBody/normalizeTriggerWhenClause/extractTriggerWhenClause directly from scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs -- no duplicated comparison logic.
AC-3: The suite runs to completion (all tests execute, none skipped/pending) with DATABASE_URL and SUPABASE_POOLER_URL both unset.

functional_requirements.requirement: TWO seeded-mutation tests, not one: clone ONE function-class fixture entry and ONE trigger-class fixture entry, deliberately alter each clone's live_text (e.g. change a compared column/token), and assert the SAME comparison now reads NOT equal for BOTH -- proving the suite can actually fail on EITHER comparison path, not merely on whichever class the single mutated entry happened to be.
functional_requirements.description: A single seeded mutation only proves non-vacuousness for whichever object class (function or trigger) it happens to mutate -- it says nothing about whether the OTHER class's assertions would also correctly fail under a real divergence (the same single-candidate discrimination gap this session has repeatedly named: a fixture/test with only one candidate proves filtering/presence, never a comparison check across the full space it claims to cover). Directly required by this session's established mutation-testing discipline and by the SD's own exit predicate.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Both mutation tests operate on in-memory clones of fixture entries, never mutating the frozen fixture file on disk.
AC-2: The mutated function-class entry's comparison (normalizeSqlBody) reads not-equal.
AC-3: The mutated trigger-class entry's comparison (normalizeTriggerWhenClause+extractTriggerWhenClause) reads not-equal.

functional_requirements.requirement: A README.md in the corpus fixture directory documenting: what the corpus is and why (RC2 normalizer-drift regression guard), how the generator script works and how to re-run it, and step-by-step instructions for hand-adding a new confirmed false positive (capture the file's own declaration text, capture the live pg_get_triggerdef()/prosrc text at the time of discovery, add an entry with confirmed_false_positive:true and a note citing its source SD/PR).
functional_requirements.description: Closes the SD scope's explicit third deliverable and gives the NEXT confirmed false positive (there will be one eventually) a durable, discoverable home instead of living only in a commit message.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: README.md exists in the same directory as the fixture file.
AC-2: README.md's hand-add instructions are followable without reading the generator script's source (self-contained).

functional_requirements.requirement: The generator script logs (never throws) each of the up-to-22 known-applied ledger paths that do not resolve to an existing file, printing each path individually -- an unresolvable path is a skip, not a fatal error for the whole generation run.
functional_requirements.description: LEAD-phase VALIDATION flagged that only a COUNT (22) was measured, not an itemized list -- itemizing at generation time gives a future reader the specific vanished paths without re-deriving the measurement.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: A generation run with at least one unresolvable ledger path completes successfully (writes the fixture for all resolvable entries) and prints each unresolved path by name.

technical_requirements.requirement: Fixture stored as a single JSON data file at tests/fixtures/apply-state-verifier-corpus/corpus.json. Generator script lives under scripts/one-off/ (or scripts/db/), with a header comment explicitly stating it is NOT invoked by CI and is a manual/on-demand regeneration tool only.
technical_requirements.rationale: Keeps the DB-touching code physically and structurally separate from the CI-run test suite, so a reviewer or future maintainer cannot accidentally wire the generator into a CI workflow.

technical_requirements.requirement: The new corpus test file imports normalizeSqlBody, normalizeTriggerWhenClause, and extractTriggerWhenClause directly from scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs -- never a re-implementation or copy of this comparison logic.
technical_requirements.rationale: A duplicated comparison function would drift from the real verifier over time, defeating the corpus's entire purpose (pinning the REAL normalizer's behavior, not a stand-in).

technical_requirements.requirement: The corpus test file has no import of lib/supabase-connection.js, @supabase/supabase-js's createClient, or any other live-DB-connecting module.
technical_requirements.rationale: Structurally enforces the SD scope's explicit 'CI needs no live database' requirement -- a grep for these imports in the test file should return zero matches.

technical_requirements.requirement: The generator script's live-text capture reuses scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs's exported resolveLive() (or issues a query byte-identical in shape, including its DISTINCT ON p.oid / t.oid tiebreak) -- never a bespoke SQL query written independently for the generator.
technical_requirements.rationale: PLAN-phase TESTING finding: a hand-rolled query that differs even subtly from resolveLive()'s real shape (e.g. missing the overload/same-named-trigger tiebreak) would let the generator capture text that the REAL verifier would never actually compare in production -- the corpus would then assert a comparison result that does not correspond to any real classifyFiles() run, silently invalidating the whole regression guard while still reporting green.

system_architecture.overview: A one-time live-DB generator produces a frozen JSON fixture; a DB-free Vitest suite replays the verifier's own exported comparison functions over that fixture on every CI run. No change to scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs itself -- purely additive regression coverage.

CI test run -> loads corpus.json (no DB) -> for each entry, normalizeSqlBody()/normalizeTriggerWhenClause() comparison -> assert equal (or not-equal, for the seeded mutation) -> pass/fail.

test_scenarios.given: The frozen corpus fixture's confirmed_false_positive:true entry
test_scenarios.then: The two are equal -- the historically-misclassified specimen stays correctly classified

test_scenarios.scenario: Every known-applied function/trigger fixture classifies as a match
test_scenarios.when: Each entry's file_text vs live_text is compared via the appropriate normalizer (function: normalizeSqlBody; trigger: normalizeTriggerWhenClause+extractTriggerWhenClause)

test_scenarios.scenario: A seeded mutation is caught on BOTH comparison paths (non-vacuity proof, function and trigger)

test_scenarios.when: The same comparison runs against each mutated clone
test_scenarios.then: Both comparisons read not-equal -- the suite is proven capable of failing on either object class, not just whichever one a single mutation happened to touch

test_scenarios.scenario: The corpus suite runs with no live database connection
test_scenarios.given: DATABASE_URL and SUPABASE_POOLER_URL both unset in the test environment
test_scenarios.then: All tests execute and pass -- zero DB-connection errors, zero skipped tests

test_scenarios.then: It completes successfully, writes the fixture for all resolvable entries, and logs each unresolved path by name

acceptance_criteria: The frozen corpus contains the sole confirmed false positive plus all 150 function/trigger-declaring known-applied files (corrected from the SD's miscited ~124), each requiring no live database at test time.

CI fails if any known-applied fixture flips away from a matching comparison, proven by TWO seeded-mutation tests (one function-class, one trigger-class) that each deliberately trigger exactly that failure.
The corpus test suite runs to completion with DATABASE_URL and SUPABASE_POOLER_URL both unset.
A README.md in the corpus directory documents how to add a new confirmed false positive.
This SD's diff adds new files only (generator, fixture, test suite, README) -- scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs itself is untouched.

risks.risk: The SD scope text's '~124' figure for the known-applied set is a miscitation of an unrelated fleet-wide census -- building the corpus from a literal reading of that figure would omit real fixtures or include the wrong population.
risks.mitigation: LEAD Explore and VALIDATION both independently measured and confirmed the real population (393/388/366/150) via two separate live re-runs producing an exact match -- the PRD scopes the corpus to the verified 150, not the miscited figure.
risks.rollback_plan: If PLAN/EXEC discover the 150-file scoping recommendation itself needs revision (e.g. a function/trigger class the regex missed), regenerate the fixture with a corrected classifier -- the generator is designed to be re-run, not a one-shot artifact.

risks.risk: A frozen fixture can go stale if a migration file is legitimately edited post-application (rare) -- the corpus would then assert a false match against text that no longer represents either side's true current state.
risks.mitigation: The corpus is explicitly a regression guard over a FROZEN pair, not a live-truth check -- the generator script exists precisely so the corpus can be regenerated when a real, deliberate change occurs; documented in the README (FR-4).
risks.rollback_plan: Re-run the generator script; the new corpus.json replaces the stale one in the same PR-review flow as any other fixture update.

risks.risk: 22 of 388 known-applied ledger paths do not resolve to an existing file -- if silently skipped without logging, a future reader could wrongly assume the corpus is complete when it is missing entries for vanished migrations.
risks.mitigation: FR-5 requires the generator to itemize (not just count) every unresolvable path in its own log output.
risks.rollback_plan: N/A -- investigating why those 22 paths vanished is an explicitly out-of-scope data-quality item, not something this SD needs to roll back.

phases.description: Build the corpus generator script: resolve the 150 function/trigger-declaring known-applied files, extract file-side text via existing exported functions, query the live DB once for the corresponding live text, write the frozen fixture with provenance (FR-1, FR-5).

Build the DB-free Vitest suite that replays the real comparison over every fixture entry, plus the dedicated confirmed-false-positive assertion and the seeded-mutation non-vacuity test (FR-2, FR-3, TS-1 through TS-4).
deliverables: New corpus test file, all tests passing with DATABASE_URL/SUPABASE_POOLER_URL unset

phases.description: Write the corpus README.md documenting the corpus, the generator, and how to hand-add a new confirmed false positive (FR-4).

technical_decisions: Scope the known-applied fixture set to the 150 function/trigger-declaring files (not the literal '~124' or a blanket 366) -- only function/trigger classification invokes the normalizer this SD guards; table/column/index-only migrations would contribute zero regression coverage for the actual RC2 concern.

Generator script physically separate from the CI-run test suite (different directories, generator has no test-runner wiring) so the DB-free CI requirement is structurally, not just behaviorally, enforced.

consumers.name: CI pipeline (unit/regression tier)
consumers.interaction: Runs the new corpus test suite on every PR/push, same as any other test file -- no new CI job or workflow needed.

dependencies.name: scripts/verify-migration-apply-state.mjs's exported pure functions
dependencies.contract: normalizeSqlBody, normalizeTriggerWhenClause, extractTriggerWhenClause, extractFunctionBodies, extractTriggerDefs are read-only imports -- this SD never modifies them.
dependencies.failure_handling: If a future change to these exports alters their signature, the corpus test suite fails loudly at import/type-check time, not silently.

dependencies.name: schema_migrations_applied table (generator-only)

dependencies.failure_handling: Generator script fails loud on a genuine DB connection error; treats an individual unresolvable file path as a logged skip (FR-5).

runtime_config.deployment_considerations: No deployment beyond the code landing on main -- new test/fixture/doc files only, zero production code paths touched.

monitoring: CI test-run pass/fail is the only observability surface -- a fixture flip shows as a normal CI test failure with the failing fixture's name in the output
observability_rollout.rollout_strategy: Direct merge to main once tests pass -- purely additive test/fixture/doc content, no behavior change to any production code path.
observability_rollout.rollback_trigger: N/A -- a failing corpus test after a legitimate normalizer change is expected and resolved by regenerating the fixture, not by reverting this SD.
observability_rollout.rollback_procedure: git revert the merge commit if the corpus itself is found to be malformed.

patterns_identified: The verifier's normalizer (normalizeSqlBody/normalizeTriggerWhenClause) is invoked ONLY on function and trigger object classes -- table/column/index/constraint classification never touches it, so a regression corpus scoped to those classes is the only population that provides real coverage for this SD's concern.

The SD scope's '~124' figure traces to a different, unrelated measurement (Alpha-3's fleet-wide potential-false-positive census, cited in SD-001's own description) -- not the schema_migrations_applied success-row count, which LEAD independently re-measured twice at 393/388/366/150.
key_decisions: Corrected the SD's miscited premise via direct, twice-independently-verified live measurement rather than building the corpus around the literal '~124' text.

Scoped the known-applied fixture set to the 150 function/trigger-declaring files, not the full 366 on-disk known-applied set -- the non-function/trigger files would add corpus maintenance weight while testing nothing this SD exists to guard.

Kept the confirmed-false-positive specimen (trg_sd_mutation_audit) as one entry within the unified 150-file corpus (it is itself one of the known-applied ledger rows) rather than a separate mechanism, with a dedicated tag and test assertion so its historical significance stays legible.
